name: Fused (best-of-breed): Probe-Wins Split-Verdict Resolver + Vendor-Neutral Workflow Spec Emission
description: Forged by workflow-forge with strategy 'best-of-breed' from bp-cnc-07-probe-wins-split-verdict-resolver (base) and bp-arc-05.vendor-neutral-workflow-spec-emission (donor). Grafted 1 of 10 donor top-level stages. This document is NOT accepted for being larger: see x_extensions.foundry.certification for the measured axis deltas that justify it, per spec _USER-PROMPTS.md:11282.

fact.description: The FACTUAL claim the lanes disagree about. Judgement disagreements (taste, priority) are out of scope - votes and councils are appropriate there.

verdicts.description: One entry per agent. A verdict whose probe block is absent is discarded, not counted.

allow_third_probe.description: Whether a mechanically different third probe may be RUN to break a genuine tie. If false, a degenerate matrix resolves UNRESOLVED.

both_states_control_required.description: Require a both-states control on the disputed detector: it must FIRE on a known-broken state and stay SILENT on a known-good one

source_workflow_path.description: The workflow to promote into a portable spec

provider_matrix.description: stage id -> vendor -> invocation. A missing cell means UNSUPPORTED, not 'the default'.

max_depth.description: The machine-readable form of the one-level-nesting rule. Fixed at 1 by design.

max_threads.description: REQUIRED WITH NO DEFAULT ON PURPOSE. The spec layer carries a live conflict: lifecycle.yaml says max_threads=4 while the owner's standing preference is to fan out large. Rather than silently inherit either value this blueprint refuses to run until the owner states one.

worker_model_floor.description: The second live conflict, also deliberately undefaulted: agent-roles/core.yaml routes worker=sonnet while the standing preference is Opus for all substantive subagents. The owner picks; the spec records the pick.

probe-extractor.description: Extracts each verdict's probe fingerprint (tool, command, field, shell) and discards any verdict that declares none

independence-analyst.description: Builds the independence matrix - which probes share a mechanism - and collapses duplicates to a single signal

tiebreak-prober.description: Runs a mechanically DIFFERENT third probe when the surviving verdicts are still split; re-running a tagged probe does not count and must never be reported as a confirmation

resolver.description: States the resolution and NAMES THE DEFECT in the losing probe; may not resolve by vote under any circumstances

owner.description: The human owner - receives an UNRESOLVED verdict together with the request for a new instrument

translator.description: Extracts the stage sequence, invariants and limits, and maps each stage per vendor

portability_critic.description: Lists what is genuinely vendor-locked instead of pretending it is portable

roundtrip_validator.description: Mechanically compares the emitted topology to the source topology

d1.owner.description: Resolves the two recorded spec-layer conflicts; the spec cannot invent an answer

routes.reason: the tiebreak probe is a real measurement and a botched one produces a confident wrong resolution

stages.title: S0 EXTRACT each verdict's probe fingerprint - a verdict with no probe is DISCARDED, not counted

work_unit.title: Extract probe fingerprints and discard every verdict that declares no producing measurement
work_unit.question_or_target: For each verdict, record the probe fingerprint (tool, command, data field, shell). Discard - do not count - any verdict with no declared probe.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the discard rule is the first place a wrong resolution is prevented

work_unit.evidence_requirement: each surviving verdict carries all four fingerprint fields; each discarded verdict is listed WITH the reason, so the discard is auditable rather than a silent drop
tests_required: a verdict with no probe block must be DISCARDED and listed, never counted as a signal
an empty probe_command must count as no probe - a fingerprint of four empty strings trivially differs from any non-empty verifier and would defeat the whole independence check
both-states control: feed one verdict with a probe (expect retained) and one without (expect discarded)
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the independence analyst confirms no discarded verdict influenced the matrix
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:WCNC-0701 emitted when probe-fingerprints.json exists, parses, and every verdict is either fingerprinted or listed as discarded with a reason; otherwise FAILED:WCNC-0701 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry - a missing probe cannot be recovered by asking again; the agent must re-run with a probe field in its contract

stages.title: S0b An undeclared source is ZERO signals, not one
S1-S2 BUILD the independence matrix and COLLAPSE duplicate-mechanism verdicts to one signal

work_unit.title: Build the pairwise independence matrix and collapse shared-mechanism verdicts
work_unit.question_or_target: For every pair of surviving verdicts, decide whether their probes are mechanically independent (different shell, different data field, different measurement). Collapse each duplicate-mechanism group to ONE signal.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: this is the step that turns six agreeing agents back into one signal

work_unit.evidence_requirement: every INDEPENDENT verdict names the mechanism that makes it independent; a pair with no named difference is CORRELATED by default (adverse inference), never independent by assumption
tests_required: six agents using the SAME probe must collapse to one signal and be flagged as such
two verdicts differing only in agent name must be CORRELATED

both-states control: build the matrix on 6 identical probes (expect 1 signal) and on 6 mechanically different probes (expect 6 signals) - a matrix that reports the same count in both states measures nothing
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the resolver confirms the collapse count before any resolution is stated
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:WCNC-0702 emitted when independence-matrix.json exists, parses, and every pair carries an independence verdict with a named mechanism or CORRELATED; otherwise FAILED:WCNC-0702 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot: mark the pair CORRELATED (the conservative direction) rather than asserting an independence that was not established

stages.title: S3 CONDITIONAL - still split? RUN a mechanically different third probe (re-running a tagged probe does NOT count)

work_unit.title: Run a mechanically different third probe to break a genuine split
work_unit.question_or_target: Design and run a probe that differs from BOTH sides by shell, data field or measurement, and report its raw output.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: max effort: a botched tiebreak produces a confident wrong resolution, which is worse than UNRESOLVED

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the third probe states explicitly HOW it differs from both existing probes (which shell, which field, which measurement) and carries its exact command plus raw output; a probe that matches either side's fingerprint is rejected as a re-run
tests_required: a third probe with the same fingerprint as an existing one must be REJECTED as a re-run, not accepted as a new signal
the third probe must state its difference axis explicitly
both-states control: submit a duplicate-fingerprint probe (expect rejected) and a genuinely different one (expect accepted)
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the resolver checks the third probe's fingerprint against both sides before using it
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:WCNC-0703 emitted when third-probe.json exists, parses, and its fingerprint differs from every prior probe on at least one axis; otherwise FAILED:WCNC-0703 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot: resolve UNRESOLVED and request a new instrument rather than re-running a probe that already failed

stages.title: S3b CONDITIONAL both-states control on the disputed detector - it must FIRE on broken and stay SILENT on good

work_unit.title: Run a both-states control on the disputed detector
work_unit.question_or_target: Run the disputed detector against a KNOWN-BROKEN state and a KNOWN-GOOD state, and report whether it fires on the first and stays silent on the second.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: a probe silent in both states measures nothing; establishing that is the cheapest way to break a tie honestly

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the control records both runs with their raw outputs and the constructed broken state; a detector that fires in BOTH states or is silent in BOTH is declared broken and its verdicts are discarded
tests_required: a detector silent in both states must be declared BROKEN and its verdicts discarded
a detector firing in both states must be declared BROKEN
a detector firing only on the broken state must be declared SOUND
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent reader re-runs the broken-state arm and confirms the detector fires
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:WCNC-0704 emitted when both-states-control.json exists, parses, and records both arms with their outputs; otherwise FAILED:WCNC-0704 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry on a broken detector - the finding IS that the detector is broken; escalate rather than re-measuring with the same instrument

stages.title: S3c A control that does not discriminate the two states cannot break a tie
S4 RESOLVE and NAME THE DEFECT in the losing probe - or return UNRESOLVED. Never a vote.

work_unit.title: State the resolution, the winning probe, and the specific defect in each losing probe
work_unit.question_or_target: State the resolved verdict, name the winning probe, and name the SPECIFIC defect in each losing probe. If no probe is independent, return UNRESOLVED with an explicit request for a new instrument.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: max effort: naming the defect is what stops the same broken probe being re-used next session

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the resolution names the winning probe and, for each losing probe, the specific defect (wrong shell, wrong data field, stale cache, broken matcher); resolved_by_majority is recorded as false and the independence matrix is attached
tests_required: 4 refute / 2 confirm where the 2 share a broken probe must resolve to REFUTED and NAME the shared defect - this is the measured historical case and the primary benchmark
6 agreeing agents using the SAME probe must be reported as ONE signal, not six
a resolution reached by counting must FAIL the never-resolved-by-majority gate
both-states control: attempt a majority-based resolution and confirm the gate FAILS; attempt a probe-based one and confirm it PASSES
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent reader confirms the named defect actually explains the losing verdict, rather than being a plausible-sounding label
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:WCNC-0705 emitted when resolution.json exists, parses, names a winning probe with each losing probe's defect, and resolved_by_majority == false; UNRESOLVED is also a SUCCESS terminal state when it names the instrument needed
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry - a second attempt at a resolution with the same evidence is the same resolution; escalate to the owner with UNRESOLVED

stages.title: S4b Majority is NEVER the tiebreak - assert it was not used
S5 OWNER resolves the two recorded spec-layer conflicts
stages.prompt: Two spec-layer conflicts must be resolved before this spec is authoritative: lifecycle max_threads=4 versus the standing fan-out-large preference, and roles.worker=sonnet versus the Opus-for-substantive-subagents preference. State which wins for each.

impact.blast_radius: writes only under command-center/resolve/bp-cnc-07/**; the third probe is a READ measurement, and a probe that would mutate state is out of contract

x_extensions.distinct_mechanism: probe-fingerprint extraction with a hard discard of unprobed verdicts, a pairwise independence matrix that collapses shared-mechanism verdicts to one signal, two CONDITIONAL stages (a mechanically different third probe and a both-states detector control) fired by when-expressions, and a terminal gate that forbids majority resolution outright
x_extensions.not_a_duplicate_because: BP-CNC-03 measures DISPERSION and never inspects a probe; this reads the probes and never computes a dispersion number. BP-CNC-04 attacks premises many lanes SHARE; this arbitrates BETWEEN agents on ONE fact. It is the only blueprint in this range whose gate asserts a negative about the resolution METHOD (resolved_by_majority == false) rather than about an artifact.
contraindications: disagreements of JUDGEMENT (taste, priority) - votes and councils are appropriate there, and this workflow would misapply an evidence standard to a preference
a single verdict - there is nothing to resolve
x_extensions.empty_fingerprint_note: The empty-probe case is called out as its own failure class on purpose. A measured defect in a sibling gate was that an absent source normalised to four empty strings, which any non-empty verifier trivially differs from - so the same-probe-rerun check could never fire and a CONFIRMED verdict with no declared source passed as corroborated. Here an empty probe_command counts as NO probe and the verdict is discarded, and empty-probe-fingerprint is an enumerated failure class.

worked_examples.name: the measured 4-vs-2 case - two agents share a broken Git-Bash probe

params.fact: the mon dispatcher is not on PATH

worked_examples.walkthrough: S0 fingerprints all six; none is discarded. S0b passes. S1-S2 finds a5 and a6 share an identical fingerprint (which / git-bash / stdout) and collapses them to ONE signal, so the tally is four independent REFUTE signals against one CONFIRM signal - not 4 versus 2. Since one side now has zero independent support for its position after the collapse, still_split is false and S3 does not fire. S3b runs the both-states control on the disputed detector: `which` in Git Bash is fed a known-present .cmd shim and stays SILENT (does not find it), proving the detector cannot see .cmd shims at all - so it is BROKEN for this question, not merely disagreeing. S4 resolves REFUTED, names Get-Command as the winning probe, and names the defect precisely: Git-Bash `which` ignores .cmd shims. resolved_by_majority is false - and note the resolution would be identical if the vote had been 2 refute versus 4 confirm, because the vote is never read.

expected_gate_outcomes.control-fires-in-both-states: PASS - the detector's failure to fire on a known-present shim is itself the discriminating result recorded by the control
expected_gate_outcomes.never-resolved-by-majority: PASS - resolved_by_majority == false, winning probe named

worked_examples.name: negative control - six agents, one probe, and an unprobed verdict

params.fact: the substrate resolves 269 distinct schema paths

worked_examples.expected_terminal_state: SUCCESS:WCNC-0705 with resolution UNRESOLVED pending a new instrument
worked_examples.walkthrough: b4 declares no probe at all and is DISCARDED with the reason recorded - four empty strings are not a fingerprint. b1, b2 and b3 share one identical fingerprint and collapse to ONE signal. independent_signals == 1 and it comes from a grep -c whose exit code is 1 on zero matches - a known unreliable counter. S3 runs a mechanically different third probe (the resolver audit, python, distinct-path set membership) which returns 234. The resolution is that the 269 figure came from one signal counted four times, and the register records the defect: a line-count over decorated values is not a distinct-path count. Had this been decided by vote it would have shipped 269 with four confirmations behind it.

benchmark_cases: 4 refute / 2 confirm where the 2 share a broken probe - must resolve to REFUTED and name the shared defect (the measured historical case)
6 agree using the SAME probe - must be flagged as one signal, not six
x_extensions.unverified: UNVERIFIED as built: fan-out-contract B4 is prose and the existing claim gate checks a single claim's probe pair rather than a multi-agent split. Settling experiment = replay the recorded 4-versus-2 case and require the correct resolution. Confidence that the failure mode is real: almost-certain (90-99%, it is measured); that the resolver fixes it given probe recording: corpus band very-likely (80-90%).
x_extensions.dependency_note: This blueprint depends on a PROMPT CONTRACT: the fan-out that produced the verdicts must have required a probe field. Without it every verdict is discarded at S0 and the workflow correctly returns nothing - which is the honest outcome, not a bug.
